goodbye.note: Often clipped to khodafez in fast casual speech.

how_are_you.note: Polite, for someone you don't know. With friends, just say Chetori? (cheh-toh-REE).

thank_you.note: Mersi (from French) is just as common and equally casual.

slang.note: Warmer, more enthusiastic thanks; fine with friends, shopkeepers, or anyone who did you a real favor. Skip in formal settings.
Literally 'may it be sacrificed for your head'; warm taarof-flavored reply for close friends or family, said with real affection rather than literally. Too intimate for strangers or formal settings.

no_problem.note: Literally 'it's not worth anything'; the go-to casual brush-off when someone thanks you for something small.

sorry.note: Bebakhshid (excuse me) also doubles as a light sorry.

of_course.note: Enthusiastic 'of course, definitely' when agreeing to do something.

cheers.note: Said when raising a glass; literally 'to health'.
